General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

The most annoying questgivers in PC games

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fallout 3's most chipper NPC, the Minnesotan menace is an inventor who sends you out on fact-finding missions to investigate the many dangers of the Wasteland.
  • Sources indicate that I think her positive outlook makes a refreshing change of pace from, you know, everything else going on in Fallout 3.
  • What I'm saying is, there are plenty of videogame questgivers much more annoying than Moira Brown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Moira Brown gets a bad rap. Fallout 3's most chipper NPC, the Minnesotan menace is an inventor who sends you out on fact-finding missions to investigate the many dangers of the Wasteland. That means she puts you in harm's way quite a lot, which many players hate her for. Others just hate her voice.

Sources indicate that I think her positive outlook makes a refreshing change of pace from, you know, everything else going on in Fallout 3. Plus she gives you an armored Vault suit just for starting her questline, and the Wasteland Survival Guide she writes with your help goes on to be a useful item in both New Vegas and Fallout 4.

What I'm saying is, there are plenty of videogame questgivers much more annoying than Moira Brown. All of the ones below, for starters. And if you disagree, you're a big meanie.

Sources indicate that rockstar loves to make us sit through cutscenes where our protagonist agrees to help out some of the most annoying people alive. Zero isn't alone—in GTA: San Andreas, he's got wannabe MC/janitor OG Loc for competition—but he is the winner for absolute worst.

It has been revealed that zero's the owner of a remote-control car shop at war with a rival called Berkley. He's a shrill parody nerd who shrieks dialogue like, "Curse you, Berkley, curse you!" Zero's most annoying mission is Supply Lines, where you pilot a model biplane to shoot Berkley's delivery drivers. The flying controls in San Andreas are terrible enough on their own (the fact it makes you complete pilot school as an unskippable part of the plot is a hate crime), but in Supply Lines you also have to cope with a limited fuel gauge that drops like a stone if you dare to use the accelerator.

Zero's excited yelling during this mission is so bad even David Cross, who voiced Zero, called it "the most annoying voice you could ever imagine" and has never finished the mission himself.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"Ignore the main questline, stick to the sidequests." This is good advice when you're playing Oblivion, if you mean "stick to the Thieves Guild, Dark Brotherhood, Daedric Shrines, Shivering Isles, and Fighters Guild," because if you take it to include the Mages Guild questline, it becomes bloody terrible advice.

The most frustrating faction in Oblivion, the Mages demand you travel to every guildhouse in Cyrodiil to earn a recommendation from each before you can join. Many of the Mages use these recommendations as a way to extort tedious favors from acolytes like yourself, such as clearing a dungeon of boring old zombies, or they involve you in silly pranks like stealing spellbooks. It's tough to pick who is the most obnoxious, but my vote goes to Falcar.

Falcar sends you to retrieve a missing ring. The ring's down a well, but turns out to be enchanted so it has an encumbrance of 150, which the previous acolyte couldn't lift. You find his body still submerged in the well. Someone drowned because of how much of a dick Falcar is.

You can drag the ring out of the well yourself, if you clear some space in your inventory and maybe drink some potions, but that turns out to be pointless. By the time you emerge from the well, Falcar's done a runner because he was secretly a necromancer this whole time. Shame his quest isn't about uncovering that, which might have been interesting, but is instead a literal fetch quest.

Before the Battinson movie reskinned The Riddler as Gotham's version of the Zodiac killer, the character was at a low point. The Arkham series saw him transform from preppy to shabby as Batman outsmarted him again and again, and by the time Arkham Knight rolled around he'd been reduced to an oily mechanic crafting racetracks to test the Batmobile, in between making Catwoman walk across his deathtraps.

Recent findings suggest that that's bad enough, but you still have to collect his trophies scattered across the city and solve "amusingly taxing" riddles by taking photos as well, and if you don't 100% all the tedious challenges he throws at you you're not allowed to see the game's "real" ending. Thanks, Arkham Knight.

It has been revealed that you're probably familiar with flyting, the medieval poetic boasting often compared to rap battles, thanks to its use in Assassin's Creed Valhalla. It was referenced a year earlier in Rune 2, but a lot less people played Rune 2.

Human Head's last game (and there's a story there), the Viking action-adventure features some truly terrible NPCs. Chief among them is Rider the Miner, who speaks entirely in rhyme with the kind of overemphasized white-ass delivery that makes you expect "My name is Rider and I'm here to say…" at any second. Instead, what you get are lines like, "When I take off my shirt you'll see all the girls flirt / Though my work is to whittle, it's my stomach that's chiseled." He's unemployed because the mine is closed, which I guess is why he's whittling? I don't know, man.

Anyway, survive all his dogshit rapping and finally you find out he's got a quest for you. Does it involve the skalds, or the bardic tradition he's part of? No, he wants you to mine some ore. Don't bother coming up with a rhyme for that, Rider.

It has been revealed that there's a lot of filler in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, but what makes it worse is how much of that filler is routed through Chadley. This tedious little twerp who looks like he stepped out of the Village of the Damned appears on your wristscreen to narrate tower-climbing, lifesprings, photorelics, summons, combat challenges, and more. It feels like you can't take five steps without him squeaking "Cloud!" and making you drop everything for an patch that could have been an email.

Then Mai appears, a gender-flipped version of Chadley who doubles the amount of dialogue you have to sit through. Instead of just having Chadley backseat driving every other sidequest, now there's a pair of squabbling siblings in the backseat who won't shut up. The third game should pull a Jar-Jar and dump Chadley straight down the memory hole, for all our sakes.

Sources indicate that the problem with Preston is that he's surrounded by some of Bethesda's best companions. Nick Valentine, Codsworth, Curie, John Hancock, cage-fighting Cait—compared to them, Preston's a personality-free zone. He's a Minuteman because he always wanted to be a Minuteman and his main function is to tell you when to clear out another settlement on behalf of the Minutemen.

Companions have an affinity score that can be raised and lowered based on your actions. Preston's affinity goes down when you do typical bad stuff, like picking pockets, stealing, taking drugs, and indulging in cannibalism, and goes up when you help settlements (of course) and modify weapons. I can feel myself getting bored even writing that out. He doesn't like cannibalism? Shocking. Give me Strong the Super Mutant any day.

Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines.

It has been revealed that the vampire prince of Los Angeles, Sebastian LaCroix runs the city from an office so gaudy it's probably got a gold-plated toilet. He talks over you, bosses you around, and if you refuse to run errands for him, uses his vampire powers to dominate you into doing them anyway. (In a nice touch, you still get dialogue options but they all say the same thing.).

When he's not bossing you around, he's whining about how difficult it is being Sebastian LaCroix. "Each minor problem like a grain of sand," he moans, "each night I inherit the desert." He doesn't even have the good grace to enjoy being rich and powerful and immortal.

Sources indicate that unlike most of the other questgivers in this list, he's not annoying because he gives you meaningless missions or wastes your time or roadblocks the best ending, but because he's written that way. You're supposed to hate LaCroix for exactly the reasons you do.

Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames, Zed Games. He's written for Rock Paper Shotgun, The Massive Concern, GamesRadar, Zam, Glixel, Five Out of Ten Magazine, and Playboy.com, whose cheques with the bunny logo made for fun conversations at the bank. Jody's first article for PC Gamer was about the audio of Alien Isolation, published in 2015. Jody edited PC Gamer Indie from 2017 to 2018, and he eventually lived up to his promise to play every Warhammer videogame.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the 75-inch Hisense U6SF Pro has dropped to $747.97 from $1,399.99 ahead of Amazon’s Black Friday sale—bringing it to its lowest price to date. The rest of the U6 Pro lineup is discounted as well, so you can pick up the same TV in sizes from 55 inches to a massive 100 inches, for anyone with the room for something closer to a home-theater-sized screen. Whichever size you choose, you’ll get free delivery to the room of choice—a service that normally costs $19.99. As for the TV itself, it’s a 2026 model that sits below the U7SG (also on sale for $1,297.99, from $1,999.99) in Hisense's lineup as the brand's entry point into Mini LED, pairing a 4K panel and local dimming with a matte, anti-reflective coating meant to cut down on glare, notes this PCMag review.

For a budget set, the U6 Pro gets a lot right when it comes to picture quality—its high peak brightness helps it hold up during a sunny afternoon in a living room with major windows, so a daytime football game or cooking show won’t look washed out, while its excellent contrast and effective local dimming keep dark scenes looking deep when you settle in for a movie at night. It also does a good job cleaning up lower-quality content, which is useful for older cable broadcasts or compressed YouTube videos—and its Fire TV interface makes it easy to jump between those kinds of content and the major streaming services without needing a separate streaming device.

Industry observers note that the U6 Pro also brings plenty to the table for gaming, with HDMI 2.1, VRR, ALLM, and a 144Hz refresh rate that PC gamers can push to 240Hz at a lower 1080p resolution. That said, the panel’s slow response time and poor motion performance can reportedly make fast-moving scenes look noticeably blurry. Viewing angles are limited too, with the picture losing quality fairly promptly when you move off-center—and its built-in speakers aren’t particularly impressive either, so a soundbar could be worth budgeting for.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Publisher 2K and developer Visual Concepts, in partnership with sister company Rockstar Games, have a collaboration between NBA 2K27 and Grand Theft Auto VI. This includes NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition, which features three-time NBA All-Star and Miami HEAT center Bam Adebayo on the cover of the limited-time collaboration, and an in-game season of content featuring Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City and MyTEAM.

“Take-Two is home to some of the most beloved series in entertainment, and this partnership unites our two biggest communities for the first time,” mentioned Take-Two Interactive CEO and chairman Strauss Zelnick in a press release. “Bringing Vice City to NBA 2K27 is a testament to the cultural impact of the games that our teams at Rockstar Games and 2K, led by Visual Concepts, have built, and we’re excited to give players an entirely new and engaging way to experience both worlds.”.

According to recent reports, starting November 27, players can pick up the NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition featuring three-time NBA All-Star and Miami HEAT center Bam Adebayo on the cover of the limited-time collaboration. In-game, Season 3 brings an extensive update with Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City and MyTEAM. The partnership also includes bonuses and access to NBA 2K27 for GTA+ Members in addition to a live activation at the “A Night in Vice City” Miami HEAT game on November 18.

The neon glow and hustle of Vice City comes to NBA 2K27 in an extended, seven-week Season 3, running November 27 through January 15 (11:00 a.m. ET). Vice City-inspired content and rewards span every corner of the Season experience, from a brand-latest Vice City-inspired Park in The City – the online social hub of NBA 2K—to a wealth of themed apparel including Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell Employee Outfits, and much more:.

NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition and GTA+ Member Benefits.

The collaboration extends even further with a one-of-a-kind cover. The NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition puts Miami HEAT superstar Bam Adebayo front and center, with cover art inspired by the neon glow of Vice City, and comes packed with Vice City-themed content. GTA+ Members can also play NBA 2K27 and unlock Vice City bonus content for a limited time.

NBA 2K27 at “A Night in Vice City”.

Finally, NBA 2K will take over 601 at Kaseya Center as the Miami HEAT take on the Milwaukee Bucks during “A Night In Vice City” on November 18. The 2K Mart meets Vice City in this immersive activation, featuring a Vice City-themed 2K Mart with limited-edition merch giveaways, and photo opportunities.

NBA 2K27 is available now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, and PC via Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches.
  • According to recent reports, per Inven Global, Harada was sitting on a panel at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea.
  • In a recent development, the panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches. This truth was reinforced recently, as he said he wished the Xbox Series S "wouldn't be released" at a developer panel. All while a member of the Xbox team was in the room.

According to recent reports, per Inven Global, Harada was sitting on a panel at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea. The panel was moderated by former Sony president Shuhei Yoshida, and featured Shift Up CTO DongKi Lee (Stellar Blade), Too Kyo Games CEO Kazutaka Kodaka (Dangenrompa), CD Projekt Red associate game director Paweł Sasko (Cyberpunk 2077), Ludeon Studios CEO Tynan Sylvester (Rimworld), and of course CEO of the newly formed VS Studio Katsuhiro Harada (Tekken).

In a recent development, the panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms. Harada led the charge, speaking to the advantages consoles provide for fighting game developers, as the hardware is ideal for tournaments and esports events. Following this, he took an opportunity to speak about a console that drew his ire.

"That said, there's something I really want to say while I have the floor. Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released," Harada said (translations to English via Inven Global). Harada then asked Sasko from the CD Projekt Red team whether he was "upset inside" because of the Xbox Series S.

Sasko proceeded to "burst out laughing" according to Inven Global, before responding: "It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly.".

Harada followed up with additional thoughts: "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say "Xbox Series S sucks," right? (laughs) Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to 'Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!' But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child.

"Furthermore, in markets like the US, there are more Series S customers than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking 'Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'".

Sasko stepped up to offer some perks to the Series S. While he agreed that many players the full technical context behind the Series S' weaknesses, he pointed out that optimisation for weaker hardware like the Series S made games run "significantly better" across all platforms. He even had a Cyberpunk 2077 example, as optimisation work done for the Switch 2 version were applied to all platforms "to great effect". Sasko also pointed to the affordability side of the argument, saying that the cheaper price of the Series S allows for market expansion.

Harada responded: "Director Paweł packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I'm worried they'll feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs).".

Here, Shift Up's DongKi Lee ended the topic with some optimism for Microsoft's future consoles: "Personally, I am looking forward to the next-gen Xbox 'Helix'. From an engineer's standpoint, if you provide us with a dev kit first in Korea as early as possible, we will put in our best efforts to develop for it.".

According to recent reports, earlier this year Harada founded Vs Studio with SNK's support, with other veterans from Bandai Namco's Tekken team hopping on board for whatever it's working on. As for the Xbox Helix consoles, in this current hardware environment with bloated costs for RAM and other components, it's reportedly looking a tad expensive. Maybe a Series S equivalent is on the cards?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is at the moment being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson stated in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Recent findings suggest that since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

A upcoming video tour of Valve co-founder Gabe Newell's $500 million superyacht, the Leviathan, reveals the surprising-among-the-wealthy fact that he treats the ship's crew extremely well.

Industry observers note that superYacht Times released a showcase of the Leviathan, which it calls "one of the most unconventional yachts ever built," earlier this month. Seemingly owing to Newell's Valve following – if top comments like "I've seen enough, Gabe deserves a third yacht" are any indication – it's already the channel's most-viewed video ever by some distance.

The Leviathan's palatial interior and industry-grade diving features have been discussed before. The striking thing about this fresh walkthrough is Newell's reputation compared to other superyacht owners.

In a recent development, "The most surprising thing is what happens when we go through these doors," editor-in-chief Francesca Webster indicates of a luxurious lounge. "Rather than having a traditional saloon, which we normally see on a superyacht welcoming guests and being the first point of contact to the interior, Gabe actually opted to utilize this incredible space for the crew mess. And he eats with the crew every day, they enjoy their meals together. And it's all about shared experience on board his boats, and that is something that we've really never seen before in our industry.".

This sentiment comes up so many times and is described with such shock that, context removed, you'd think Newell had grown a third arm out of his forehead. Among super-wealthy superyacht owners, it's evidently quite uncommon to support and engage with crewmates to this degree – to the point that, SuperYacht Times reports, Newell is keeping staff for 4.5 years on average while ships of this class average just six to nine months tenure.

"One of the most unique things about Gabe, the ownership structure that he has, and the way that he has a vision for yachting, is that this VIP cabin is also used by the crew," Webster adds. "That's a pretty special thing. I don't think I've ever seen a crew cabin that looks quite like this.".

In a recent development, elsewhere, the ship has 15 PC gaming stations "for the crew, the guests, and Gabe himself to come and enjoy themselves. This is also where they do training and crew development, so if anyone on board wants to up their skills, this is where it happens, which is an incredibly special thing." This is, presumably, where Newell plays Dota 2 nowadays.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

"If it wasn't clear enough that this is an owner who loves his people, this is going to blow your mind," our narrator indicates before introducing the sort of bedroom that the crew would use.

Generations before Wiimote waggling, the accessory was designed to bring nascent motion control to the NES. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to billion-dollar franchises, you tend to think of blockbuster movies with significant budgets that pack theaters around the world. However, why be so limiting in your thought process? NCIS, which premiered in 2003 and is presently in Season 24 on the 2026 TV schedule, is a franchise that has generated $10 billion in sales over its lifetime on TV. From advertising to licensing deals and merchandise, its enduring appeal has catapulted its status into a level that few TV franchises will ever attain.

While we are at a point where I can’t really remember TV without NCIS, due to its long-running and always-expanding presence, I have to admit I was absolutely stunned by the $10 billion figure Bloomberg reported. Sure, the Law & Order franchise gets a ton of attention, and I think everyone knows its “Dun Dun” sound effect, but NCIS has also maintained an astounding level of popularity for over two decades. I mean, even Mark Harmon’s exit couldn’t bring NCIS down.

As George Cheecks, the co-chair of Skydance TV, said, NCIS is a "quiet hero." It might not seem like the major hit on the surface; however, if you look at the numbers, it "dwarfs" so much.

With 24 seasons of the flagship series and multiple spin-offs, it’s easy to reflect on how the blend of its popular procedural format, workplace comedy elements, and characters to care about has led to success that other TV shows will never achieve.

It has been revealed that it’s wild how the most-watched upcoming show on TV this fall is the latest installment in the franchise, NCIS: New York, which put Special Agent Sam Hanna back in the mix. Being a spinoff of a successful and beloved show is not a guarantee of success, with NCIS: Los Angeles, NCIS: New Orleans, and NCIS: Hawaii all having fallen by the wayside. But the New York installment is off to a great start, and NCIS: Origins and NCIS: Sydney bring the current number of programs set within the same world that are right now on the air to four. However, this success didn't happen immediately.

Sources indicate that in September 2003, when NCIS debuted as a spin-off of JAG, it took a bit of time to find its footing. It ultimately gained popularity across much of Europe and in Australia, which helped lead to licensing deals with TV networks and streaming services. As ratings climbed, spin-offs started to multiply, and the money kept coming in, hence the billion-dollar number that has left me flabbergasted.

Clearly, it’s hard to wrap your head around $10 billion. I mean, it's an unattainable number for most. But when it comes to the business of television, indicates like NCIS, Law & Order, Chicago Fire, FBI, and Fire Country have a formula that works and makes them appealing to very large portions of the population in the U.S. and abroad, so their success and continued expansion make sense.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in late October, Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games announced that it was in trouble. Funding for its ambitious, historical sandbox strategy had suddenly been pulled, and as a result the studio was at "real risk of closing". But it turns out the situation was even more dire than the announcement suggested, as Raw Power Games declared bankruptcy on the same day.

Despite this, development of Chronicles: Medieval will continue with at least some of its original creators involved, after Satisfactory owners Coffee Stain Group swooped in to purchase the assets and IP.

In a press release, Coffee Stain mentioned that it submitted the winning bid in Raw Power's sale process following the company's bankruptcy, paying 36.75 million Danish Krone (around $5.42 million) for Chronicles: Medieval's intellectual property.

Rather than acquire the assets directly, however, Coffee Stain will transfer them directly to a "newly established firm" that is owned 75% by Coffee Stain, and 25% by "a small group of key members of the game's original development team." Alongside paying full purchase price for Chronicles: Medieval's assets, Coffee Stain will also fund the continued development of the game.

Industry observers note that in a statement, Coffee Stain CEO Anton Westbergh mentioned that "Chronicles: Medieval made a strong impression at its reveal at Summer Game Fest last year. We're happy to step in and help bring it to players after the recent developments in Copenhagen." He also explained that "Things have been moving fast around this deal, and our short-term focus will be on working out how best to complete the game, together with the new tech giant's management team.".

Chronicles: Medieval is in the top 30 most wishlisted games on Steam, higher than the likes of Guild Wars 3, Atomic Heart 2, and the upcoming Mass Effect-like Exodus, so it's clear why this was an attractive proposition for Coffee Stain. What isn't clear from all this is how this affects Raw Power's existing staff. Presumably, Coffee Stain will seek to transfer as many people from Raw Power as they can, given they've been working on the game for years and therefore understand it intimately. But there's nothing in Coffee Stain's statement that confirms this.

According to its Steam page, Chronicles: Medieval is still slated for an early access release in 2027, but it isn't clear at this juncture whether the acquisition will affect this. In its press release, Coffee Stain states that "further information about the intends for the game, including the release timeline, will be communicated through the game’s own channels in due course.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that good Fun Corp, the studio made up of the original developers behind Hell Let Loose, has finally announced a release date for its anticipated next project: Hunger. The extraction shooter-slasher game enters early access on Steam on 3rd December, and there's good news if you're eager to try it out before then.

Industry observers note that hunger's first and only open beta has also been announced, taking place 27th-29th November, the weekend prior to its early access launch. Unlike past tests, this one is available for anyone who requests access on Steam.

Sources indicate that though it may appear as yet another extraction shooter on the surface, Hunger offers more complex and intertwined systems than most. For one, combat has a focus on melee with only a few intentionally clunky firearms available. Though this is a PvPvE game, the vs environment side includes the sort of puzzle-solving, questing and dungeon-raiding typical of RPGs. The game's alternate history, plague-ravaged European setting gives it a grimey, steel-and-mud look few games have.

Beyond the in-match experience, Good Fun's ambitions extend to Hunger's MMO-style progression, its hub area with distinct characters and varied playable classes - all of which can be sampled in the upcoming beta.

Hunger just came off a very successful closed beta, which clearly didn't suffer by kicking off right alongside Modern Warfare 4's DMZ early access. Hunger is currently among Steam's most-wishlisted games, with over 700,000 wishlists, according to the developer.

The launch version includes three large maps, six playable characters, and five Mastery trees with more than 100 Masteries to unlock for your characters. Hunger has only been unveiled for PC so far, but will presumably arrive on consoles following its early access journey.

#4503. ChatGPT's New GIF Generator Is Fun, but Won't Replace Us Humans (Yet)

ChatGPT's New GIF Generator Is Fun, but Won't Replace Us Humans (Yet)

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (610 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to generating AI images, both Gemini and ChatGPT do a passable job.
  • It has been revealed that openAI is pitching the fresh feature as an animation tool, not exactly as a way to create looping videos—though that’s how I ended up using it.
  • Industry observers note that AI art can be quite sterile, but I was surprised by how adding motion and animation to the mix makes generating images a lot more fun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to generating AI images, both Gemini and ChatGPT do a passable job. In most cases, the results will look AI-generated, but they likely won’t have glaring spelling problems or missing limbs. Now, OpenAI is trying something newly introduced, introducing GIF support for ChatGPT. It's the organization's first "moving images" feature since OpenAI shut down Sora, and while you can generate hyper-realistic videos in Gemini, this new ChatGPT feature is trying to fill in the gap, in a small way.

It has been revealed that openAI is pitching the fresh feature as an animation tool, not exactly as a way to create looping videos—though that’s how I ended up using it. You give ChatGPT a prompt, as detailed as you can make it, and the chatbot produces a GIF in just a few seconds. You can start with your own drawings or images, too. ChatGPT uses sketches as the base for animations, though it can turn any still image into animated GIFs. Like other AI editing tools, you can edit it if ChatGPT didn't quite get it right: You can ask ChatGPT to make the GIF longer or shorter, remove certain objects, change the style, slow down transitions, among other edits.

Industry observers note that AI art can be quite sterile, but I was surprised by how adding motion and animation to the mix makes generating images a lot more fun. Unlike traditional GIFs, which usually pull from existing video clips, you can turn anything you want into a GIF, which is especially cool if you're using your own art. In my testing, I found this to be the most rewarding part. It’s not always possible to one-shot a GIF with a single prompt. But after a few rounds of edits, I ended up creating some GIFs that I actually wanted to share in my WhatsApp groups.

That being stated, I think human-made GIFs are still the gold standard here. For example, I asked ChatGPT to generate a video of someone brewing a pour-over, with a gooseneck kettle, showing the coffee blooming process. It did okay, but it’s nothing like actually making a pour-over. The kettle doesn’t move in circles, the water doesn’t rise evenly, there are no bubbles, and the steam is all over the place.

Compare that to the GIF below, which comes from a royalty-free video. Even though it’s a compressed, low-quality, and noisy GIF, it still shows the movement of the pour, the water rising, and even the bubbles. The details captured by a real video just aren’t there in ChatGPT GIFs. If that’s what you’re expecting, you will be disappointed. But I don't think that's the point of this feature anyway.

Industry observers note that I found that ChatGPT excels when you’re making something fun, and you don’t look into the details too much. It pulled off a loop of a cat playing with a ball, and it was great at making a festive GIF for Diwali. It even made a GIF based on a photo. I asked it to create a fun promotional GIF for my JBL Bluetooth speakers, and it did the job quite well. At first, the transitions were too jarring, and the movement just made no sense. After some editing, though, I got it to a decent place.

Still, the main issue with ChatGPT GIFs is that complex movement and transitions aren’t nailed down. A hand shifts position weirdly between frames, and colors and objects appear out of nowhere. But if you can get over these issues, you can make some fun, lighthearted GIFs and memes to share with your friends on Instagram or WhatsApp.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Industry observers note that kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

Sources indicate that 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the organization contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

In a recent development, earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent manufacturer Take-Two swiftly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Sources indicate that hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely indicates anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I imagine most BioWare fans would argue that the studio's peak happened somewhere between Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect 2. For me, though, the absolute high point was Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and I was always a little bitter that the devs moved on to create Mass Effect rather than finishing Revan's story in a proper KOTOR 3. That's why seeing Casey Hudson, original director of KOTOR, return with a spiritual successor in Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic is so exciting, and it's apparently been a long time coming.

"It is really a dream project for us," Hudson says in an interview with The Fourth Curtain podcast. After leaving BioWare – for a second time – in 2020, he founded a newly introduced studio called Humanoid Origin, which was developing a "sci-fi action RPG" that would've been a "brand-new IP." That studio shuttered in 2024 after an "unexpected shortfall of funding," leaving Hudson to figure out what to do next.

"We had lots of ideas, including, like, 'Do we get funding to continue with what we were doing? Are there other paths forward?' But over the years – myself and folks from our team, we worked on the original Knights of the Old Republic way back in the day, and since then BioWare also had the Old Republic MMO. So we've kept up connections with folks at Lucasfilm," he states.

Recent findings suggest that some time after Humanoid Origin shut down, Hudson explains, "the head of Disney Games reached out and said, 'Hey, what if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games? The spiritual successor.'".

Hudson notes he'd been "circling" the idea of returning to KOTOR for some time. "It's something that I would love to do, but I was either doing other things or other projects. There were times when maybe it wasn't right for Lucasfilm, or they weren't ready for it. There wasn't really a fit.".

He was excited both by the possibility of returning to KOTOR and bringing back "some of the the top folks we've worked with," but surviving a studio shutdown leads you to "become the most skeptical person on earth," he says. "You don't really trust anyone to follow through with a deal or funding until things are signed, done, and legit.".

Getting those contracts finalized is how Hudson spent "the first half" of 2025. Then he spent the rest of the year "just starting to assemble our team, doing a prototype, and then creating the announcement trailer.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Yes, that means that Fate of the Old Republic had only barely entered development at the time of its reveal at The Game Awards last year, but Hudson seems confident we won't be waiting forever for it to be finished. The team works "at a very brisk pace," and he claims we should expect "new announcements" sometime next year.

Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic could be going for "a more simple hero's journey" to avoid BioWare's "self-indulgent" storytelling, says ex-Dragon Age boss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally coming out worldwide next week, putting an end to a 13-year wait and at least one popular meme format, but the highly-anticipated game might look a bit different in Japan.

Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

In a recent development, PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

Recent findings suggest that the potential regional censorship isn't too surprising, though, considering how trimmed down GTA 5's Japanese release was at the time. Rockstar had to remove and alter a bunch of GTA 5 scenes to comply with the country's normally strict content guidelines, including Trevor's controversial torture segment and multiple scenes featuring nudity. Baldur's Gate 3, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and many more have been subject to similar restrictions in the past.

Earlier this week, GTA 6 became the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation and Xbox's history. That's also not a huge surprise, either. The juggernaut game's lavish marketing blitz took over London's Selfridges and Rockstar is even hosting an entire music festival starring a couple A-listers.

10 Shows Like 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' You Should Watch Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following the dramatic conclusion of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners way back in 2022, the show has returned for a new season set in the megalopolis of Night City with a standalone story and a new cast of characters (by necessity).

  • According to recent reports, an iconic, effortlessly cool genre classic, Cowboy Bebop is one of the undisputed GOATs of anime, blending western, noir, and crime genres and setting the resultant mash to a killer soundtrack of old-school jazz (which serves much the same purpose as Cyberpunk's propulsive electronic grooves).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following the dramatic conclusion of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners way back in 2022, the show has returned for a new season set in the megalopolis of Night City with a standalone story and a new cast of characters (by necessity).

Though the aesthetic and themes of cyberpunk have their roots in American science fiction of the 1970s and '80s, anime and manga of the '90s and beyond embraced the form and took it to entirely fresh places—so much so that a Japanese/Polish co-production of an adaptation of a video game from a Polish designer has taken its cues from a couple of decades' worth of great anime and cerebral sci-fi. Which is to say, if you're looking for more heady sci-fi series, these 10 are a good place to start.

According to recent reports, an iconic, effortlessly cool genre classic, Cowboy Bebop is one of the undisputed GOATs of anime, blending western, noir, and crime genres and setting the resultant mash to a killer soundtrack of old-school jazz (which serves much the same purpose as Cyberpunk's propulsive electronic grooves). The title's "cowboys" are bounty hunters in a near-future in which humans have been forced to colonize the solar system after Earth became uninhabitable. Different settings, but both highlights offer up ragtag crews with highly dubious fates. Former hitman Spike Spiegel leads his crew on one nearly disastrous mission after another, their standalone adventures all building to a thoroughly memorable climax. Stream Cowboy Bebop on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

This one's set in 22nd-century Japan, with a slick Blade Runner-esque aesthetic and a setup reminiscent of Minority Report. Here, technology exists to measure intentions, so crimes can be stopped before they’ve occurred, at which point the “criminals” are placed into psychological treatment (à la A Clockwork Orange)—or subject to summary execution because their threat potential is too high. That ability to predict behavior bleeds over into every aspect of life: careers and even relationships are determined in large part by the same systems that sniff out criminal intent. Obviously, this is all perfectly fine, and there’s no potential for abuse or miscalculation whatsoever...though there are a couple of warning signs. The first involves a new Enforcer who becomes a potential murderer himself when he miscalculates the extent of a criminal’s potential to do wrong, and, even more significantly, the existence of a criminal mastermind who is somehow invisible to the tech, even as his criminal actions grow more and more elaborate. Stream Psycho-Pass on Prime Video and Crunchyroll.

Created by Tim Miller and with director David Fincher as an executive producer, this animated anthology series is a grab bag of wildly diverse offerings: Each episode is produced by a different international studio, with the only link between them being one of the three words in the show's title. One episode deals with robotic gladiator fights in dystopian London, another finds us under the threat of sentient yogurt, yet another finds an ambitious cat learning to make use of a family's robot helper. Its format dictates that no two episodes are going to have the same premise, but it shares with Cyberpunk an edgy sensibility and stories set in an apocalyptic future, albeit with a dark sense of humor—its four seasons offer up a mix of tech, sex, violence, and gorgeous animation. Stream Love, Death & Robots on Netflix.

One of several completely standalone spinoffs of the wildly influential 1995 film (itself based on the beloved manga series), Stand Alone Complex requires no prior knowledge. The style is largely the draw, as the series luxuriates in its fictional Nihama City setting, a world unto itself in a future Japan in which cybernetic people hack directly into the internet. Our sympathies are more with the authorities—in this case, Public Security Section 9, a cybercrime and antiterrorism police unit—than the cyber criminals, but the show approaches some of the same themes as Edgerunners with legit punk style. Stream Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex on Tubi and The Criterion Channel.

In this adaptation of the Richard K. Morgan cyberpunk classic of the same name, Joel Kinnaman and Anthony Mackie (yes, both of them) star as Takeshi "Tak" Kovacs. In this future megacity setting, human consciousness can be transferred between bodies. The tech is widely available, but only the wealthy can afford the backups and protections that make it a form of virtual immortality. Kovacs is a former soldier turned mercenary, revived from a backup after 200 years by Laurens Bancroft (James Purefoy), one of the wealthiest men alive. His motives for bringing the man back are shrouded in mystery, but he's giving Tak a chance to solve a very cold case: his own murder. Stream Altered Carbon on Netflix.

Another popular (and Emmy-winning) game adaptation, Arcane is based on League of Legends, a top-down actioner involving online opponents shooting lasers across a map. It doesn't sound like fodder for a show this impressive, but here we are. The League of Legends lore forms the backdrop for the show, but the pull is in the narrative involving two sisters caught up in the growing conflict between a utopian city and its oppressed underclass, without whom it couldn’t exist. The painted animation style is truly something special—not a stylistic match for Cyberpunk, but the two reveals both go far above and beyond to create striking visual worlds. Stream Arcane on Netflix.

According to recent reports, vash the Stampede is a hunted outcast with a dark history that slowly comes to light over the course of the series. He’s got a reputation as a human wrecking ball, bringing destruction wherever he goes, and seemingly just for fun—but in reality he’s far more respectful of life than his pursuers. Still, cities evacuate at the mere possibility of his arrival, and a huge bounty sits on his head (no matter that the bounty hunters do far more damage than Vash). He and his friends—actually a couple of insurance agents—find themselves in a series of misadventures on the planet Gunsmoke, building to a final showdown that caps the series with finality. Visually, it’s probably one of the defining ‘90s shōnen-style action series, with elegantly choreographed gunfights that never get old. Tonally similar, Trigun also shares with Cyberpunk 2 the work of legendary composer Tsuneo Imahori, his music being crucial to both demonstrates. Stream Trigun on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

Another from animation studio Trigger, Darling in the Franxx leans heavily into the mecha sub-genre, set in a post-apocalypse where children are bred and indoctrinated into piloting the title's massive Franxx to defend the remnants of humanity. Adults are pretty much immortal, so the kids simply don't have any other utility. Two of these teens begin to develop romantic feelings for each other, potentially complicating their usefulness to society and leading to an explosive, bittersweet finale. Stream Darling in the Franxx on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that what starts out as a relatively straightforward action show about space bounty hunters (the title's “Killjoys”) develops surprising depth over the course of its five seasons. As officially sanctioned Killjoys, the trio at the show’s heart (Hannah John-Kamen, Aaron Ashmore, and Luke Macfarlane) are bound to remain politically neutral at any cost. Initially, that’s a way to get them right into the heat of a fight, but as they develop ties of friendship and family in an exploited community, they come to understand the high cost of unchecked wealth and greed, and the ways in which neutrality always benefits the oppressors. The show’s creators make exceptionally good use of a limited budget and offer up some impressive queer rep along the way, a rarity in pop sci-fi. Stream Killjoys on Tubi or buy it from Prime Video and Apple TV.

According to recent reports, another great cyberpunk metropolis: here it's Kansai, an increasingly lawless city run by elite criminals known as Akudama. An ordinary girl, quite inadvertently, becomes caught up in a major planned heist and is forced to fake credentials as a master swindler in order to stay alive. Like Cyberpunk, the show tackles anti-authoritarian themes among a diverse crew of outsiders. Stream Akudama Drive on Cunrchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

In a recent development, the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the tech giant of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

According to recent reports, finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Manufacturer chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

Once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

In a recent development, so, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

Industry observers note that in the meantime, Bethesda isn't letting Skyrim's 15th anniversary go by without a few celebrations. For one, the seminal role-playing game is deeply discounted on all platforms, in the very unlikely scenario you haven't tried it out yet.

According to recent reports, the Elder Scrolls Online Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim is also joining the festivities by adding the Greymoor Chapter into the base game for free, giving everyone access to a few famous Skyrim locales and more. A brand-latest, separate Golden Pursuit campaign will let you earn some Skyrim-centric goodies up until 2nd December, as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, at long last, the transfer of power is complete. Dune: Awakening, Funcom's ambitious survival MMO based on the classic sci-fi novel, has completed is pivot away from massive multiplayer, and can now be played fully offline.

The offline function arrived in an otherwise unremarkable patch that mainly fixes specific bugs and technical concerns. "It's now possible to play the game in single-player mode without requiring an internet connection at any point, including creating and deleting single-player characters.," Funcom revealed in a Steam post.

Dune: Awakening has been gradually drifting away from being a purely multiplayer experience for some time. In April, Funcom made its PvP element, like the Deep Desert and shipwreck exploration, fully optional. A fully fledged single-player mode arrived in September, including a dramatic rework of several major endgame systems—like its dynamic political "Landsraad" system' to make them work in solo play. At that point, single-player still required an Internet connection. Now though, that's no longer the case.

To be clear, Dune: Awakening can still be played with all its multiplayer and PvP trappings, now including a "Go Online" button for exactly that purpose. Nonetheless, it's been a fascinating shift in direction, one that, alongside games like Marathon, embodies a broader apparent trend away from large-scale. competitive multiplayer experiences toward smaller, cooperative communities. Whether with friends or alone, players increasingly want to be able to live in their own worlds, unbothered by the wider, more tumultuous encounters of the open Internet.

Whether this is a positive shift is up for debate—encounters with strangers on the Internet can provide highs as well as lows—but it's certainly an interesting one. Either way, offline mode isn't the end of Dune: Awakening's journey. A fresh expansion is coming in December, one that lets players explore Arrakis' frozen poles in a radically different scenario from the base game. Funcom appears to be in it for the long term with Awakening too, having recently pivoted to focusing purely on support for it and its other multiplayer survival game Conan: Exiles.

Industry News: Each upcoming GTA moves the series closer and closer to the original Mafia, the open-world game that bettered Rockstar

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer.
  • Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.
  • Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be declared, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a new GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

The influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

In a recent development, the city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

Much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

Back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

The Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on Upcoming Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group.

The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

Recent findings suggest that "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler said in a press release.

Recent findings suggest that black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the firm swallowed up countless big names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024.

Industry observers note that it doesn't sound like Black Forest split with the rights to the Destroy All Humans series or its permanently mean alien protag Crypto, but the studio has remarked it's still working with THQ Nordic in some capacity. The original Destroy All Humans run nosedived wildly in quality after the second game, so I'm not sure how exciting a remake of, let's say, Destroy All Humans: Major Willy Unleashed would be nowadays, though I'd definitely be interested in seeing Crypto again in another ridiculously silly, sometimes rude and anarchic adventure.

Five Smartwatch Heart Rate Zone Hacks Every Runner Should Know

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you've spent any time in or around running culture over the last few years, you've undoubtedly encountered someone preaching the gospel of Zone 2 cardio.
  • To train by heart rate, you aim to keep your heart rate in the "zone" that gives you the desired workout.
  • Pace can be a distraction during easy runs, especially considering all the different variables that affect your effort, like hills, humidity, and general fatigue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you've spent any time in or around running culture over the last few years, you've undoubtedly encountered someone preaching the gospel of Zone 2 cardio. Legend has it that easy, conversational effort cardio—also known as cardio that takes your heart rate into "Zone 2"—is the secret to unlocking everything from a bigger aerobic engine to faster race times and even a longer life.

To train by heart rate, you aim to keep your heart rate in the "zone" that gives you the desired workout. The catch is that Zone 2 is easy to get wrong, especially since no one can agree on what it actually means. Your smartwatch can show you your heart rate, but many recreational runners will still drift into a “gray zone” that's too fast to be truly easy, and too slow to give them a real workout. If you're struggling to hit Zone 2 consistently, there are a few smartwatch hacks that can help.

Pace can be a distraction during easy runs, especially considering all the different variables that affect your effort, like hills, humidity, and general fatigue. A 9:30 mile might be Zone 2 on a flat, cool day and Zone 4 on a hot, hilly one.

Dig into your watch's activity settings (on Garmin, it's Activity > Data Screens; on Apple Watch, the Workout app's metrics layout; on Coros, Polar, and Suunto, similar menus) and put live heart rate zone front and center, ideally as a zone number or colored gauge rather than just a raw bpm figure (though this assumes these zones are accurate—more on that below).

Create an alert when your heart rate goes above or below a target range, delivered as a vibration pattern, a beep, or both. Set the alert for the upper boundary of Zone 2, and you've essentially hired a mini coach who taps you on the wrist whenever you get overzealous. Whenever you hear or feel that buzz, you’ll know you need to ease into a slower jog until your heart rate settles.

Industry observers note that instead of free-running and checking your numbers afterward, build structured workouts that carry the targets for you. In Garmin Connect, TrainingPeaks, Apple's Custom Workout feature, Coros Training Hub, or similar platforms, you can create sessions like "10-minute warm-up in Zone 1, 40 minutes in Zone 2, 5-minute cooldown" and sync them straight to your watch.

During the run, your watch displays the current step, the target range, and whether you're above, below, or in the pocket. Many will automatically advance between intervals and alert you when it's time to shift gears.

This is especially powerful for:.

Heart rate-based intervals, like 4 x 4 minutes in Zone 4 with Zone 1 recovery, where you don't have to do mental math or check the clock.

Progressive long runs that start in Zone 2 and finish in Zone 3.

Hill repeats, where pace is meaningless but effort matters.

Most watches calculate default zones using a generic formula like 220 minus your age, which can be off by 10 to 20 beats for any given individual. If your zones are wrong, your Zone 2 training isn't Zone 2 training.

Here’s how to fix your watch’s heart rate zones:.

Sources indicate that find your true max heart rate. The informal way is to just notice what number you see on your watch when you can no longer speak comfortably; the more formal way is this treadmill test. You can also look through your recent hard efforts, like races, hill repeats, or all-out intervals, and see the highest sustained heart rate you've recorded.

Use lactate threshold heart rate instead. Many watches can estimate this automatically after a few hard efforts, and zones built from threshold tend to be more personalized than ones built from max.

Customize the boundaries. Dive into the heart rate zone settings and input your own numbers. Some runners prefer the "MAF" method (180 minus age, with adjustments) for aerobic base building, and most watches let you set that as a custom range.

In a recent development, recheck every few months. Fitness changes, and so do your zones.

A screen crowded with cadence, vertical oscillation, ground contact time, running power, and lap pace is a recipe for second-guessing.

In a recent development, create a dedicated Zone 2 data screen with just two or three fields: current heart rate zone, elapsed time, and maybe distance. Turn off auto-scroll so it doesn't flip to a screen full of numbers you don't need. If your watch supports multiple activity profiles, make a separate "Easy Run" profile with this stripped-down layout and keep a different profile for tempo days and races.

A chest strap (or a forearm or upper-arm optical band) is generally more accurate and responsive than the wrist-based sensor on your watch. For heart rate training, where a few beats can mean the difference between Zone 2 and Zone 3, I recommend buying one. This COOSPO heart rate monitor is one of my favorites, and it's only $31.99.

The bottom line: Your smartwatch can make heart rate training far easier, but only if you set it up to support you rather than overwhelm you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Resident Evil series creator Shinji Mikami says the debut title from his new studio Unbound is on track to release next year.

Recent findings suggest that mikami said as much during an appearance on a Japanese podcast last month, but his comments seem to have slipped under the radar until Twitter account Genki shared them. The interview is entirely in Japanese with no official translation, but according to machine translation, Mikami says the game will be out somewhere around the middle of 2027.

According to recent reports, that is unfortunately the only clear-cut aspect of this story, as everything else starts getting really confusing the deeper you dig. News of Unbound's formation didn't become widely circulated until March of this year, but the studio's official website says it was established in 2022, which is before Mikami left his previous studio, Tango Gameworks, the team behind The Evil Within, Ghostwire Tokyo, and Hi-Fi Rush. The website itself is also an overstimulating mess of cryptic, flashing imagery, Japanese and English-language text, and a broken countdown clock.

And then there's Kamuy, another studio Mikami apparently founded after his time at Tango. In 2024, Automaton reported on comments made by Mikami during a talk show indicating he was done with the survival horror genre and wanted to focus on games with shorter release cycles led by young talent. It's unclear if Kamuy has simply been renamed Unbound or if they're two distinct entities, but we haven't heard a word about Kamuy in years.

Recent findings suggest that separately, there's been some conflicting information about the nature of Unbound's debut title. Mikami's longtime collaborator Masato Kimura described the game as "a AAA title for high-end consumers," but in this upcoming(ish) interview, Mikami states it's a relatively small game. Again, it's machine-translated, but that definitely would conflict with the idea of a premium, big-budget AAA game.

It has been revealed that unbound was acquired by Stellar Blade developer Shift Up in 2026, so it stands to reason that funding isn't an issue in terms of overall scale, but the latest comments from Mikami seem to indicate a smaller release. All that is to say, we know virtually nothing about this game beyond the fact that it's apparently coming in 2027. Whether it'll be another survival horror game like Mikami is known for or something completely different, I suppose we'll find out next year.

Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami believes devs need to "make games that leave people wanting to clear them with their own hands" rather than being content watching a playthrough.

If you fantasize about twisting your affinity for words into more traditional combat, the creator of Universal Paperclips has just the game for you. Blending together the fundamentals of Scrabble, tower defense strategy games and some roguelike seasoning, Towers of Babble is perfect for the logophile looking for a more bespoke Scribblenauts.

Each campaign in Towers of Babble begins with a handful of letter tiles. Spell a noun and you can build a unit on the map. Like larvae in an anthill, words are predeterminedly assigned to harvesters or defensive units. Spell out verbs and modifiers to create power-ups for your nouns. Use your harvested resources to purchase upgrades, such as a larger selection of tiles or adding premium stats to certain letters. Survive enough waves of enemies and youâll have conquered the level, itself assigned to a upcoming word, and can carry over certain elements to your next struggle session.

According to recent reports, created by alternative indie dev Frank Lantz, best known for the absurdist industrial simulator Universal Paperclips, Towers of Babble boasts 120,000 levels and some 200,000 word units to choose from. Many words have loose affiliations to their definitions. The semiotics conjure its own form of magic, imbuing units with healing elements, poison clouds of chip damage, stronger shields, bigger blasting super missiles. Compounding words together into long-winded, Germanic strings of nonsense. While each “Librarian” plays alone, they fight this war together. Each conquered word contributes to the same massive tower. What happens when each is cleared, and this lexicon reaches the heavens, is anyoneâs guess.

Even prior to the interview finally airing in full, we know the man felt his You Can See Everything portrayal was “crazy.” And I’m not even talking about whatever happened with that shower scene.

Recent findings suggest that per Evans, Gutman is actually a bit behind the times. The journalist asked about the project we see in the documentary, a project that had Evans and Holmes attempting to fix the technology that led to Theranos dealing with legal troubles by approaching the problem in a different way. According to the scientist, that project is dead, and it’s dead for one significant reason: The tech was too expensive.

According to recent reports, no. I am not working with Elizabeth on [my current project]. Key distinction from the movie: That was a different idea. Completely different technology.

Gutman interrupted and asked, “So, we’re talking about Theranos 3 now?” Evans shook his head, and responded:.

Sources indicate that it’s not Theranos. At the time we were filming, we were talking about basically using microscopes, taking really good camera images of bacteria, and then using computer vision like driverless cars use to determine that’s a car, that’s a bus, that’s a person… So, that was kind of the idea. Turns out, that the cost was just too high.

Shortly after Holmes was in prison, they scrapped the idea we see them chatting about in You Can See Everything. Despite the way the now-infamous egg scene portrays Evans, he remarked here he spent about seven months worrying about the kids and life in Texas. Where the kids would go to preschool, what hotels to stay at while visiting Holmes in prison.

Then, he got back to it. Now, he is still working on "the problem," but he feels his research is not the same thing.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Once I finally settled and I regained like my strength and my energy back, I started thinking about, ‘Well, that last one didn’t work. But how could it? And my background’s in photonics, lasers. You know it’s a big thing in the movie, lasers. So I started reading research papers, and I’m now working with a group of scientists and other people to solve the same problem in a different way.

Ultimately, from what Evans seems to be saying, the former happened, though the latter did not pan out as expected.
